root_cause: The bare `catch {}` inside the device-load useEffect swallows relay fetch errors. The slotMap silently falls back to local-only devices and the UI renders with no indication that the relay was unreachable, so the user may believe an incomplete device list is complete.
fix_summary: Capture the relay-fetch failure into component state and render it using the existing inline `bg-destructive/10 text-destructive` error-box pattern (same as actionError). Keep the non-fatal policy: local devices still render.
allowed_changes: src/components/DevicesTab.tsx — extract the pure load logic into a testable helper that returns { entries, relayFetchError }; add relayFetchError state; set it in the (formerly bare) catch; render it with the existing inline destructive error-box pattern, guarded so local devices still show.
src/components/DevicesTab.loadDevices.ts (new) — pure, dependency-free load helper extracted from the useEffect, so it can be unit-tested in the repo's existing node/vitest idiom.
constraints: Do NOT add a toast library.
Do NOT add jsdom / @testing-library/react or any component-rendering stack — the repo tests pure logic in node/vitest; match that idiom by extracting the load logic.
Do NOT change the non-fatal policy: a relay failure must still render local devices.
Minimal surface: no refactors beyond what the fix requires.
Preserve the existing loadError (fatal) vs relay-fetch (non-fatal) distinction.
non_goals: IdentityPanel.tsx:198 may have the same bare-catch pattern — observe and report, do NOT fix (out of scope).
No change to forget-device flows or the slot extraction helpers.
No change to the relay request shape or marmot-ts calls.
